title: Processing: Getting "In" to Empty
coreMove: Take one captured item at a time and decide what it is, whether it is actionable, and where it goes next.
sourcePressure: Processing means clarifying each collected item one at a time, deciding whether it is actionable, and moving the in-basket toward empty through decisions.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Reviewing the in-basket repeatedly as if looking at items counts as deciding them.
sourceAnchorNote: The source sidecar contains no chapter-specific named people, named studies, or named places. Use only the listed GTD terms, official metadata, or supported artifacts; do not invent anecdotes.

sourceAnchors.name: Getting "In" to Empty
sourceAnchors.detail: The locked title and sidecar define the chapter goal as emptying the in-basket through clarification.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Empty does not mean finished with life; it means every captured item has been decided enough to leave the basket.

sourceAnchors.name: actionable versus non-actionable split
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar names this distinction as central to processing.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The first question is not priority; it is whether the item asks for action at all.

hook: stress is not about having too much to do
a messy desk proves the system is broken
counterintuition: the real problem is not time but attention
this is not about doing more but doing what matters
the simple move is actually the powerful one
tryThisNow: set a timer and write everything down
pick one task and make it specific
review your list and choose a priority
examples: timestamp plus name plus laptop plus decision repeated across all six examples
home kitchen clutter as mental-load shorthand

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: a city animal-control office after a weekend complaint surge
exampleSpecs.audience: a dispatcher facing dozens of captured reports
exampleSpecs.stakes: a dangerous-dog complaint could sit beside routine noise notes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 9:12 a.m., Rachel takes the top report only, decides whether it requires action, and refuses to scan the rest of the stack for comfort.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stamped complaint form on top of a wire tray

exampleSpecs.domain: a craft brewery production office sorting supplier emails
exampleSpecs.audience: a production manager with captured requests from malt, keg, and label vendors
exampleSpecs.stakes: a missing label approval could halt canning day
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The office smells like wet grain while Michael turns one vendor email into either trash, reference, waiting-for, or a next action.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a malt invoice curled beside a can label proof

exampleSpecs.domain: a public radio newsroom clearing pitch notes after morning meeting
exampleSpecs.audience: an editor with story ideas and source callbacks captured in one inbox
exampleSpecs.stakes: a time-sensitive interview could be lost if notes remain vague
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Is this a story, a someday idea, or a call we owe today?" Juliette asks before moving the note out of in.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a reporter notebook open under a studio clock

exampleSpecs.domain: a marina office processing winter storage forms

exampleSpecs.stakes: a boat could be hauled without the right owner approval
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The shrink-wrap rolls are stacked by the door while Anders shows the difference between a pile reviewed and a pile emptied by decisions.

exampleSpecs.domain: a small customs brokerage processing shipment exceptions

mustAvoid: drifting into prioritization rather than clarification

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

tryThisNowSpec: Pull one item from an inbox and write only one label: actionable, non-actionable, waiting for someone, or reference.
